## Review — PR #11323 · substance **ACCEPT** · ⛔ flip deferred (CI still converging)

Net 48 deleted / 7 added across two files. Mechanical, as the ruling required. The review turns on one question, and it was answered properly.

### The ablation — the only thing that could have made this PR worthless

A dedupe's real risk is never that the suite goes red. It is that **the suite never exercised the helper**, in which case repointing it at a different implementation proves nothing and the green run is a tautology dressed as evidence. This is what I asked to be settled, and it was settled correctly:

Predicted **in writing before running**: mutating the shared `totp()` must fail inside `beforeAll`, at the enrolment confirmation, because that is the file's first consumer of a TOTP.

Measured:

```
FAIL |isolated| test/two-factor-lockout.dogfood.test.ts (beforeAll hook)
AssertionError: verify-totp (enrolment): {"message":"Invalid code","code":"INVALID_CODE"}: expected 401 to be 200
```

⇒ **The suite genuinely drives the shared helper.** Not a tautology.

And the part that makes the ablation a statement about *this change* rather than a generic observation:

> Pre-change the same mutation could not have moved this file at all — it referenced `./totp.js` nowhere, which is the contrast that makes the ablation a statement about the new wiring.

That is the control I would have asked for, supplied without being asked. Marker counts checked in both directions (injected 1, original removed 0), restore byte-identical by `git hash-object` on both sides, re-run to a real green, and the mutation ran under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` so an interrupted run could cost a reading but never leave the tree mutated.

⚠️ **Two deviations from the prediction were reported rather than smoothed over**: the rejection is `401 INVALID_CODE`, not the `400` predicted, and vitest accounts a `beforeAll` failure as *1 file failed / 5 skipped* rather than *5 failed*. Location and cause matched; the numbers did not. Reporting a prediction that was partly wrong — instead of quietly rewriting it to match — is the behaviour that makes the rest of the report worth trusting.

### The Zone-2 falsification I asked for

I flagged that the dangerous case was **divergence** between the two implementations, since a "mechanical dedupe" that silently changes behaviour is the worst outcome here. That was checked *before* anything was touched: function bodies extracted and diffed, exactly one difference each — the `export` keyword. **No divergence.** Nothing behavioural rode in under the dedupe.

### Unprompted, and correct: the stale comment was repaired in the same commit

The shared module's header warned that the lockout file "still carries its own private copy". That statement **goes false with this commit**, so it was replaced rather than left to rot. Nobody asked for that. It is the docs-drift discipline — *does my change make an existing statement untrue?* — applied to a code comment, which is exactly where that discipline is usually skipped.

### Gates, and a contrast worth naming

`check:type-check-debt` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (`@objectstack/service-knowledge` had no built type entry point). The dev treated that as **NOT MEASURED, not a pass**, built the closure, and re-ran to the gate's own verdict line: *"33 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 449.8s, 1897 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number."* 18 families, every one exit 0, at `3c6028f1b2`.

Worth recording alongside its sibling card: **#11076's PR resolved the same gate differently** — it *declared a narrowing* rather than running it, on the grounds that the full workspace build was disproportionate to a one-file diff and the shared verify lock was contended. Both are honest handling. Neither is the failure mode that matters, which is calling `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` a pass. One measured it; the other declared it unmeasured and said why. Both acceptable; the difference is worth seeing side by side.

Similarly, this PR correctly concludes **no `dist` preflight applies** — `test/totp.ts` is a relative sibling compiled from source by vitest and `@objectstack/dogfood` declares no `build` script — while #11076's ablation *did* require a rebuild, because that suite resolves its subject from `dist`. Knowing which situation you are in is the whole game there; a blanket rule either way would have produced a false result in one of the two.

### One semantic nuance, stated rather than hidden

The collapsed URI block previously guarded with `expect(uriSecret, 'no secret in the otpauth URI').toBeTruthy()`; `secretFromTotpUri` throws with the same message instead. Same red/green outcome, thrown rather than asserted. The card sanctions this collapse explicitly, and it was flagged rather than buried.

### ⛔ Why this is not a flip yet

CI on `3c6028f1b2`: **32 checks, zero failures**, but the run had barely started — six `Test Core` shards, three Dogfood gates, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and four Type Check lanes all still in progress. Green is read **by job name** when the run finishes.

**Clause-②: no** — confirmed against the landed diff. Two test files, no production code, no behaviour change. `skip-changeset` correct: `@objectstack/dogfood` is `"private": true` and publishes nothing.

## Precision correction to my own review — "control" overstated it, and the dev drew the line I blurred

In my review (`5385756173`) I described the pre-change contrast as *"the control I would have asked for, supplied without being asked."* That word is wrong, and the implementer's own report is more careful than my summary of it:

> `pre_change_contrast`: **Not measured, and not claimed as measured.** Argued from grep instead: pre-change the lockout file referenced `./totp.js` nowhere (the only importer was `two-factor-backup-code-reveal.dogfood.test.ts`), so mutating the shared module could not have moved it.

**"Control" implies a measured leg.** This one was not run — no mutation was applied against the pre-change file to observe it staying green. What exists is an argument from absence-of-import, and it is a sound one: a module the file does not import cannot reach it, and that absence was established by grep rather than assumed. But an argument and a measurement are not the same evidential object, and this lane's whole method depends on not letting the second word stand in for the first.

**The conclusion is unaffected** — the ablation still establishes that the suite drives the shared helper, because that leg *was* measured and went red in the predicted place. What changes is only the strength claimed for the supporting half: the ablation is a statement about the new wiring by argument, not by a second measured leg.

Recording it because the implementer drew this distinction explicitly and unprompted, and my review flattened it. A report that says "not measured, and not claimed as measured" is doing exactly what this lane asks for; a reviewer who then upgrades it to "control" undoes that work in the summary everyone actually reads.

No change to the verdict: substance **ACCEPT** stands, and the PR stays draft pending CI.

## Landing verdict — PR #11323 flipped ready and enqueued

CI on `3c6028f1b2`, read **by job name**: **35 checks, all completed, zero failures.** All six `Test Core` shards, all three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and all four Type Check lanes green — `Type Check · debt ledger` included, matching the local `--re-measure` verdict the dev reached after refusing to record its `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` as a pass.

Enqueued through the merge queue. `Fixes #11111` closes this card on merge.

The package now holds **one** spelling of RFC 6238 where it held two, with the hand-rolled rationale preserved in the shared module and the stale duplication warning removed in the same commit. Net 48 deleted / 7 added.

The verdict rests on the ablation, not on the green: mutating the shared helper reddens the lockout suite in the predicted place, so the file genuinely drives what it now imports. A dedupe whose suite never exercised the helper would have been green too — and worthless. Standing correction on record (`5385764528`): the pre-change leg was **argued from absence-of-import, not measured**, and my review overstated it as a "control".
